# `silk/io/logger`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The `Logger` effect: log messages with a level, a template, and values.

## When to use
Require `&mut Logger` in code that logs, and call `Effect.logInfo`, `Effect.logWarning`, and the
other `Effect.log...` functions. The program decides where the messages go when it provides the
logger: `silk.io.logger_native.StderrLogger` for a native program, or [`InMemoryLogger`](#InMemoryLogger) in a test.

## Details
Each call has a [`LogLevel`](#LogLevel), a template that is known at compile time, and a borrowed tuple or
record of values. The template rules are those of `silk.text.format.Format.format`. The provider
formats the message and decides about newlines, timestamps, and prefixes. The caller does not
need a `Writer` or an `Allocator`.

[`InMemoryLogger`](#InMemoryLogger) keeps at most eight messages and 64 message bytes in total. It counts calls
that failed separately from messages that it kept.

## Errors
- [`LogError`](#LogError) if the provider cannot log the message. The message was not necessarily logged.

## Gotchas
The accessors of [`InMemoryLogger`](#InMemoryLogger) need an event index less than [`Logger.length`](#Logger.impl.length) and a byte
index less than the message length.

## Examples
### Log a warning and check it in a test
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.io.logger { LogError, LogLevel, Logger }

pub effect fn main() -> i32
  ! LogError {
  let mut logger = Logger.inMemoryProvider()
  let values = .{ kind: "users", count: 3 }
  run Effect.logWarning("cache {kind} missed {count} times", &values)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Logger>(&mut logger)
  if Logger.length(&logger) != 1 || Logger.levelAt(&logger, 0) != LogLevel.Warning {
    return 1
  }
  if Logger.messageLengthAt(&logger, 0) != 26 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="Logger"></a>

## `Logger`

```silk
pub service Logger
```

The effect that receives log messages with a level, a template, and values.

### When to use

Require `&mut Logger` in code that logs, and call `Effect.logInfo`, `Effect.logWarning`, and the
other `Effect.log...` functions. The program decides where the messages go when it provides the
logger: `silk.io.logger_native.StderrLogger` for a native program, or [`InMemoryLogger`](#InMemoryLogger) in a test.

### Details

The caller does not need a `Writer` or an `Allocator`. A provider implements `log`. It formats
the message with the rules of `silk.text.format` and decides where it goes and what decoration it
gets, such as a newline or a timestamp.

<a id="Logger.log"></a>

### Operation `log`

```silk
effect fn log<Args>(
    level: LogLevel,
    static template: string<'static>,
    args: &Args
  ) -> () ! LogError ? &mut Logger
```

Formats `template` with `args` and logs it at `level`.

#### Details

The template rules are those of `silk.text.format.Format.format`, and the compiler checks them. The
call adds no newline, level label, or timestamp. The provider can add them.

#### Errors

- [`LogError`](#LogError) if the provider cannot log the message.

Interpret this code only with knowledge of the selected provider. Different providers can use
the same code for different failures.

<a id="Logger.impl.inMemoryProvider"></a>

### Associated function `inMemoryProvider`

```silk
pub fn inMemoryProvider() -> InMemoryLogger
```

Creates an empty in-memory logger with capacity for eight events and 64 message bytes.

#### Gotchas

A call fails when eight events are already committed. A call also fails when its bytes exceed
the remaining 64-byte total. Neither failure commits the event.

<a id="Logger.impl.inMemoryProviderFailAt"></a>

### Associated function `inMemoryProviderFailAt`

```silk
pub fn inMemoryProviderFailAt(failAt: usize) -> InMemoryLogger
```

Creates an in-memory logger that rejects one zero-based attempted-call ordinal.

#### Details

The configured attempt increases [`attempts`](#Logger.impl.attempts) but does not increase [`length`](#Logger.impl.length) or consume
message capacity. Other attempts retain the eight-event and 64-byte limits of
[`inMemoryProvider`](#Logger.impl.inMemoryProvider).

<a id="Logger.impl.length"></a>

### Method `length`

```silk
pub fn length(self: &InMemoryLogger) -> usize
```

Returns the number of events that the in-memory logger committed.

#### Details

Failed attempts do not increase this count. Use [`Logger.attempts`](#Logger.impl.attempts) when rejected calls must
also be observed.

<a id="Logger.impl.levelAt"></a>

### Method `levelAt`

```silk
pub fn levelAt(self: &InMemoryLogger, index: usize) -> LogLevel
```

Returns the severity of one committed event.

#### Gotchas

`index` must be less than [`length`](#Logger.impl.length). An unused index below eight returns the initial Trace
value instead of trapping. An index of eight or more traps.

<a id="Logger.impl.messageLengthAt"></a>

### Method `messageLengthAt`

```silk
pub fn messageLengthAt(self: &InMemoryLogger, index: usize) -> usize
```

Returns the UTF-8 byte length of one committed message.

#### Gotchas

`index` must be less than [`length`](#Logger.impl.length). An unused index below eight returns zero instead of
trapping. An index of eight or more traps.

<a id="Logger.impl.messageByteAt"></a>

### Method `messageByteAt`

```silk
pub fn messageByteAt(
    self: &InMemoryLogger,
    eventIndex: usize,
    byteIndex: usize
  ) -> u8
```

Returns one UTF-8 byte from a committed message.

#### Gotchas

`eventIndex` must be less than [`length`](#Logger.impl.length). `byteIndex` must be less than [`messageLengthAt`](#Logger.impl.messageLengthAt)
for that event. An unused event or invalid byte index traps. An event index of eight or more
also traps.

<a id="InMemoryLogger"></a>

## `InMemoryLogger`

```silk
pub struct InMemoryLogger
```

A deterministic [`Logger`](#Logger) provider that retains up to eight events and 64 total message bytes.

### When to use

Use this provider in tests that must inspect event order, severity, message bytes, or failure
behavior without process output.

### Details

The provider copies each committed message into fixed internal storage. It records attempted
calls separately from committed events. Capacity failure and configured failure do not commit an
event.

### Gotchas

The accessors need an event index less than [`Logger.length`](#Logger.impl.length) and a byte index less than the
message length.
